newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco forecasts GDP rise over 10 pct for 1966.
newsitem.headline: Morocco forecasts GDP rise over 10 pct for 1966.

text.p: Morocco's gross domestic product (GDP) will increase by more than 10 percent by the end of 1996, the official MAB agency said.
This follows a GDP fall of 7.6 percent last year, and earlier forecasts of around 11 percent rise for this year.
Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj presented the forecast to a cabinet meeting late on Thursday night, MAB said.

He said global monetary reserves had increased to three billion dirhams ($344.8 million) at the end of July 1996 while public savings had reached 5.7 billion dirhams, a rise of 2.6 billion dirhams compared with the end of August 1995.
After a period of stagnation in the first six months this year, total credits of 3.6 billion dirhams had been granted in July to the farming and housing sectors.
"Bank deposits recorded an important increase, reaching 3.7 billion dirhams in...July after a fall during the first six months of the year," Kabbaj was quoted as saying.
All economic indicators showed "the resumption of economic activity", he said, including the main indicators on the Casablanca bourse. ($1 = 8.7 dirhams) -- Rabat newsroom - 212-7-726518
